arc_intro:
FQ-203 — Deepak Menon (DevOps Lead)

I want a full audit trail before we close this thing out. The HighErrorRate alarm was correctly firing for 6 months into a silent SNS topic, and I want to know exactly when that subscription was removed and by whom — not to blame anyone, but because if it was an accident, I want to understand how it happened so we can structurally prevent it.

While you're setting up CloudTrail properly, also tell me whether what we're looking for is even IN there. I have a feeling FoodQuick hasn't been capturing everything everywhere.

— Deepak
arc_outro:
Deepak Menon (DevOps Lead)

A contractor cleaned up what they thought was their own personal notification — understandable. Nobody told them they were the only subscriber. And because CloudTrail was single-region, we almost missed it entirely.

That's the full story: alarm configured correctly, real incidents in Week 14, contractor removed the last subscription shortly afterward without realizing the consequence, nobody noticed for four months because there was nothing left to notice. Not malicious, not careless — just the kind of thing that happens when there's no process for it.

Ravi has the timeline. One last thing to set up: a real observability dashboard, so we're never guessing about state from individual metrics and logs again. That closes out FQ-203.

— Deepak

tasks.scenario: Deepak wants to find who removed the SNS subscription. Before querying anything, you need to check what CloudTrail is actually set up to capture in this account.
tasks.question: What's the first thing to verify before assuming CloudTrail can answer this question?
options: A) Nothing — CloudTrail automatically captures all API calls in all regions for all AWS accounts from day one

B) Whether a trail exists, and whether it covers the right regions — CloudTrail trails must be explicitly created and configured, and by default, the management console may show recent events from a limited event history, but a true, persistent, queryable trail requires deliberate setup
C) Whether the AWS account has been active for at least 12 months, since CloudTrail only becomes available after that period
D) Whether Deepak has admin IAM permissions, since only admins can ever access CloudTrail events
tasks.explanation: CloudTrail automatic not — trail explicitly create must do, region coverage configure must do. in Console 90-day event history default-a visible-a is there, but persistent, queryable trail (long-term retention, all-regions) deliberate setup is needed.
tasks.ren_correct: Correct — trail explicitly create must do, automatic full coverage not.
tasks.ren_wrong: A bit think again — CloudTrail automatic all-regions coverage kudukkkathu. Trail create must do, coverage check must do first.

tasks.question: What's the difference between CloudTrail MANAGEMENT events and DATA events?
options: A) They're the same thing, just two names used in different regions

B) Management events record API calls that manage AWS RESOURCES (creating/deleting S3 buckets, modifying security groups, removing SNS subscriptions — the 'control plane') and are included in the free tier. Data events record API calls on the DATA inside those resources (S3 object-level GetObject/PutObject, Lambda invocations) and cost extra — most security auditing needs management events, not data events
C) Data events are free and management events cost extra — the opposite of their actual billing
D) Data events only apply to RDS and cannot be enabled for S3 or Lambda
tasks.explanation: Management events — resource manage doing (create, delete, modify — control plane), free in tier included. Data events — resource's for data API calls (S3 object level, Lambda invocations), extra cost. Most security audit (SNS subscription removal like we're looking for) management events.
tasks.ren_correct: Correct — management events control plane, free. Data events data-level access, extra cost.
tasks.ren_wrong: A bit think again — billing reverse-a thoughthikitiya. Management events free tier, data events extra cost.

tasks.question: What does enabling a CloudTrail trail as 'multi-region' actually do, compared to a single-region trail?
options: A) A multi-region trail costs significantly more and is only needed for accounts with resources in many different regions

B) A multi-region trail automatically captures events from ALL AWS regions — including regions the team doesn't actively use — so API calls from any region are logged in one place, even if a resource was inadvertently created or modified in an unexpected region. A single-region trail only captures events from that one specific region
C) Multi-region trails capture events faster than single-region trails, with no other functional difference
D) There's no practical difference — CloudTrail automatically replicates all events to the primary region regardless of trail configuration
tasks.explanation: Multi-region trail ALL regions's events a in place capture does — team-a actively use do regions also including. in C5.4 we in us-east-1 forgotten Lambda kandupidichom — this exact same principle: unexpected in region any nadandha, multi-region in trail visible will happen.
tasks.ren_correct: Correct — multi-region trail all regions cover does, single-region only that one region.
tasks.ren_wrong: A bit think again — multi-region trail just speed difference not. Coverage difference — ALL regions vs one region real difference.

what_to_find: The trail is single-region (ap-south-1 only) — API calls from any other region are not captured in this trail, which directly limits what we can find about the SNS subscription removal if it happened from or via any other region
CloudTrail log retention is also set to 'never expire' in S3 — same pattern as the CloudWatch Logs retention finding from C6.1, costing money for indefinite storage

SNS is a regional service — the order-service-alerts topic is in ap-south-1, meaning the subscription removal API call should be in the ap-south-1 trail, but the single-region limitation is still a real gap for future events in other regions
Data events are not enabled, which is appropriate for now (management events are what we need for this investigation)
tasks.correct_fix: Convert foodquick-main-trail to a multi-region trail so all future API calls from any region are captured. Also set a retention policy on the CloudTrail S3 bucket (e.g. 1 year for compliance/security audit purposes, specific to that need). Query the existing trail for the SNS UnsubscribeFromTopic event before changing anything, since the SNS topic is in ap-south-1 and should be in the existing trail.

tasks.scenario: While reviewing CloudTrail logs, Deepak asks whether the trail can also show who originally created the HighErrorRate-order-service alarm — to understand its full history. You search the trail for the CreateAlarm API call.
tasks.diagnosis: CloudTrail cannot provide records from before the trail was first enabled — it has no retroactive visibility into API calls that happened before it started logging. This is expected and not a bug, but it creates a genuine audit gap: anything that happened before the trail was set up (in this case, 4+ months of account history before the trail existed) is permanently unrecoverable in CloudTrail, regardless of the trail's current configuration.
tasks.fix: Accept this as an expected limitation and document it honestly: the alarm's original creation predates the trail, so its creator and original configuration decisions are not in CloudTrail. For events from before the trail, any other available records (PR history, Slack messages, internal wikis, commit logs) may provide partial context, but CloudTrail cannot help here. This underscores why continuous, multi-region CloudTrail coverage from day one matters — retroactive setup cannot recover historical records.
tasks.explanation: This CloudTrail's real limitation, important-a theriyanum — trail enable do then only records will be, retroactive-a historical events recover to do cannot. This 'start early' importance's exact lesson — later enable did, before's records forever gone.

cases.case_1: An account where the team needs to know every time ANY IAM role or user is created, modified, or deleted
cases.case_2: An account where compliance requires logging every single S3 object download from a specific sensitive bucket
cases.case_3: An account where the team wants to know when security groups are changed, but doesn't need object-level S3 access logs
cases.case_4: A new AWS account being set up from scratch, where the team wants maximum future audit capability from day one

correct_answers.case_1: Management events only, multi-region trail — IAM events are management events (control plane), covered by default in a properly-configured trail at no extra cost beyond S3 storage
correct_answers.case_2: Data events specifically on that S3 bucket — object-level GetObject events are data events, not management events; these cost extra per event but are the only way to log individual object downloads
correct_answers.case_3: Management events only, multi-region trail — security group changes are management events (control plane API calls), no data events needed
correct_answers.case_4: Multi-region trail with management events enabled immediately, data events only where specifically needed for compliance — establishing coverage from day one means no audit gaps for future events, even if data event scope is expanded later

tasks.scenario: Deepak asks for the cost breakdown of a proper CloudTrail setup: management events trail + S3 storage for 1 year of logs. FoodQuick generates roughly 50,000 management events/month. CloudTrail charges: first copy of management events is FREE per region; S3 storage for the log files at roughly ₹1.92/GB-month; estimated 50,000 events generates approximately 0.5GB of compressed log data per month.
tasks.question: What's the real monthly cost of running a properly-configured multi-region management events trail, and is it justified?
tasks.solution: Management events: FREE (first copy in any trail). S3 storage: ~0.5GB/month × ₹1.92 ≈ ~₹0.96/month for current event volume. Even at 10x event volume (500,000 events/month), S3 storage would be ~₹9.60/month. Total multi-region management events trail: effectively free at any reasonable volume, with S3 storage costs negligible. Framed for Deepak: the cost of properly-configured CloudTrail from day one is nearly zero — the cost of NOT having it was four months of undetectable monitoring failure and two unresponded real incidents. This is one of the clearest 'insurance that costs basically nothing' cases in AWS.
tasks.explanation: CloudTrail management events cost nearly zero — S3 storage only real cost, that a bit. This 'almost free insurance' — not having it's real cost (undetected incidents, no audit trail) very very adhigam.
